messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a cluster of late-enqueue spikes around 10:12, a bunch of requests showed +150-300ms before they hit the coalescer queue.
alan: ouch. any pattern on tenant or payload size?
jun: mostly small text gen requests from the mobile cohort, tenant=payments-prod, bursty at ~500rps.
alan: can you paste the logs?
maria: log snippet:
```
2026-03-21T10:12:04Z INFO enqueue_delay_ms=210 stream_id=abcd tenant=payments-prod route=/v1/generate
2026-03-21T10:12:04Z INFO coalesce_slot_wait_ms=35 batch_size=8
```
jun: looks like late-enqueue, not coalesce delay. they waited before being enqueued.
sam: are we sure it's not client retry storms? client traces show single attempts.
ops-bot: deploy completed 10:10:58 — rolling windows bumped coalesce grace to 40ms (flag: batch.grace=40ms)
tara: related to the recent deferred-ack experiment? we started ack-on-dequeue to reduce requeues.
maria: yes — deferred ack means producers keep connection open longer, so we only ack after final acceptance. that reduced churn but may hide enqueue latency.
alan: tradeoff: immediate ack => clients think request accepted (good) but we must safely requeue on host crash. deferred ack => better correctness but increases perceived enqueue latency and complicates tracing.
jun: in this run deferred ack combined with autoscaler spin-up created a delay window where requests sat in front of the coalescer.
sam: suggestion: emit an explicit metric 'enqueue_visibility_ms' = time from client send -> visible_in_coalesce (sampled). start with 1% sample.
tara: +1. also add a tag for deferred_ack=true so we can split histograms.
alan: for traces add two timestamps: client_send, enqueue_observed. MUST be cheap (span drop sampling).
maria: another thought — add an early prefix ack when the request is accepted by admission (so client sees accepted) but still keep deferred final ack for durability; that would decouple client latency from internal staging.
jun: early prefix ack is nice but brittle: if admission ack is returned, client might stop retrying even though we later OOM and drop. need a clear SLA on retry semantics.
tara: RFC follow-up: define semantics for prefix-ack vs final-ack, failure modes, and client contract. propose ticket INFR-342 to track.
alan: operationally, we also need better dashboards: queued_depth_by_tenant, queued_age_p50/p95, deferred_ack_ratio.
sam: I'll prototype a small prometheus exporter to compute queued_age using the new enqueue_observed field and push a per-tenant summary.
maria: until we have metrics, quick win: add warn log when enqueue_delay_ms > 100ms including tenant and request size. keep sampling.
ops-bot: added label: ticket INFR-342 created by tara.
jun: for long term: consider a two-stage admission — fast accept buffer (low durability) for latency-sensitive tiny requests and a slow path for big ones. keeps coalescer-fed fast.
alan: that's basically a hot-lane idea. we need admission priority and tight isolation to avoid starvation.
tara: action items: (1) sam add enqueue_observed tracing & queued_age metric (2) maria add warn log for >100ms (3) jun draft prefix-ack semantics for INFR-342 (4) alan sketch hot-lane admission constraints.
maria: thanks — will follow up with a short beta on staging tomorrow. :thumbsup:
